title: MCCE: A Framework for Multi-LLM Collaborative Search in Discrete Spaces with Similarity-Filtered Preference Learning
claim: A closed-loop system couples a frozen LLM and a trainable LLM, evaluated and refined through preference learning on stored experience.
layout: 3 stacked bands, cyclic green arrows, clockwise flow, hand-drawn icons
description: A cyclic system diagram in three horizontal bands with a hand-drawn, doodle style. The top green band covers user interaction. An elderly-user icon with a speech bubble sits beside boxes labeled 'optimized results' and 'problem formulation', with a Q&A bubble and an SQL database icon for initialization. The middle blue band is candidate generation. On the left, a dashed box holds 'llm api' and 'llm local' robot icons joined by a 'collaboration' icon. In the center, a 'verifier' box with a checklist sits above 'pareto selection', with circular sync arrows. On the right, a red-hatched candidate pool shows DNA, a terminal and molecule icons. The bottom green band covers update and learning: breakthrough experience, similarity-based data synthesis, and DPO training. Large thick green arrows link the bands in a loop, and the eye goes first to the center and then follows the arrows.
caption: Overview of the proposed MCCE framework. The system starts from user interaction and population initialization based on the problem definition and evaluation criteria. During candidate generation, a frozen API-based LLM and a trainable local LLM collaboratively propose new molecules. These candidates are assessed by the multi-objective evaluation module, which applies Pareto-based selection to maintain a balanced population, while breakthrough solutions are stored as experience. In the update and learning stage, similarity-based data synthesis constructs preference pairs from historical trajectories, and the local model is refined via DPO training. This process forms a self-improving feedback loop in which global exploration (API LLM) and local adaptation (trainable LLM) co-evolve toward progressively optimized solutions.
abstract: Multi-objective discrete optimization problems, such as molecular design, pose significant challenges due to their vast and unstructured combinatorial spaces. Traditional evolutionary algorithms often get trapped in local optima, while expert knowledge can provide crucial guidance for accelerating convergence. Large language models (LLMs) offer powerful priors and reasoning ability, making them natural optimizers when expert knowledge matters. However, closed-source LLMs, though strong in exploration, cannot update their parameters and thus cannot internalize experience. Conversely, smaller open models can be continually fine-tuned but lack broad knowledge and reasoning strength. We introduce Multi-LLM Collaborative Co-evolution (MCCE), a hybrid framework that unites a frozen closed-source LLM with a lightweight trainable model. The system maintains a trajectory memory of past search processes; the small model is progressively refined via reinforcement learning, with the two models jointly supporting and complementing each other in global exploration. Unlike model distillation, this process enhances the capabilities of both models through mutual inspiration. Experiments on multi-objective drug design benchmarks show that MCCE achieves state-of-the-art Pareto front quality and consistently outperforms baselines. These results highlight a new paradigm for enabling continual evolution in hybrid LLM systems, combining knowledge-driven exploration with experience-driven learning.
